title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
authors: A. Radford, J. Kim, T. Xu, G. Brockman, C. McLeavey, I. Sutskever
before: Speech recognition models were trained on small curated corpora and fine-tuned per domain.
problem: They broke on accents, noise and languages outside their training set.
breakthrough: 680,000 hours of weakly supervised multilingual audio, trained as a single sequence-to-sequence model.
why: It made robust open speech recognition a commodity, which is the input side of every voice assistant built since.
next: Voice interfaces on top of LLMs, then natively audio-capable models like GPT-4o.
inherits: Speech as just another sequence task for a transformer.
